title: UET: dissect and verify CRC
description:
Add a "has_crc" pref (default true) to tell us whether we expect packets
to have CRC at all (this is an out-of-band network-wide configuration).

Add a separate "validate_crc" (default false) for the computation part.

Optional spinoff: !25611 

AI-Assisted: no

Signed-off-by: Alex Badea <alex.badea@keysight.com>

notes.body:
Sample capture, also includes ICMP to verify we get encapsulation right  [uet-crc-ip-and-icmp.pcap](/uploads/fc8b301503cb8326b99dc307a1dce74e/uet-crc-ip-and-icmp.pcap): 

```
./run/wireshark -o uet.has_crc:TRUE -o uet.validate_crc:TRUE -d ip.proto==253,uet uet-crc-ip-and-icmp.pcap 
```

Using the larger pcap [from here](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22094#note_2854693562) `../tools/fuzz-test.sh uet--pds-all-udp.pcap` is up to:

```
Pass 102:
    Fuzzing packets 2416-52416 of 64998
    uet--pds-all-udp.pcap: (-nVxr) (-nr)  OK (4 seconds)
```
This larger PCAP uses UDP and shows invalid checksums.  Do you plan on fixing that within this MR?

I have a hunch that PCAP did not actually have correct CRCs.

I was planning on addressing UDP (and IPv6) in a later MR, but since you've raised me IPv6 support, I'll try to come up with good PCAPs.

I've contrived [uet-generated-crc-encaps.pcap](/uploads/2802308af62606aaeaa78fc4ea3760cc/uet-generated-crc-encaps.pcap) using this [uet_gen_encaps.py](/uploads/8bf8ab3356ead4305226581c31d126c3/uet_gen_encaps.py) ghetto scapy script.

I've also run it through

```
$ ../tools/fuzz-test.sh uet-generated-crc-encaps.pcap 
...
Pass 1643:
    uet-generated-crc-encaps.pcap: (-nVxr) (-nr)  OK (0 seconds)
```
Before this the dissector MUST `#include "config.h"`

So for `uet` dissector, we only really need to know "is there UDP before UET" or not -- and in IPv4 we could look at `ip_proto == 17`, but IPv6 is more hairy.

But I believe it would suffice to check if we find `proto_udp` towards the tail of `pinfo->layers`, and then we don't need the IP proto number.

I don't quite understand this.  Is UET only taking the CRC of the "layer immediately preceding it" (which could be UDP or IPv4  (if no UDP)).  From the current code, I thought if UET was over UDP, the CRC would be IPv4+UDP+UET (not UDP+UET).  If UET is only taking CRC of the "layer immediately preceding it", then yes this logic needs to be improved.

This is also why I tried to make uet_compute_crc() more generic.  Unsure if dissect_uet_common() will also need to be refactored to handle where the CRC data is coming from (passed in by dissect_uet/dissect_uet_entropy)

> if UET was over UDP, the CRC would be IPv4+UDP+UET

That is correct -- _with UDP's checksum forced to 0_ for computing the CRC.  That's why I'll need to know if there's UDP in there.  (spec is at https://ultraethernet.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2026/01/UE-Specification-1.0.2-1.pdf section "3.5.25 UET CRC", with the computation steps on page 343;  I tried to summarize the important parts at [the top of `uet_compute_crc`](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/25143/diffs?commit_id=39137bf60741b9411df49b5c0f475e30638c68c8#7ff0044177febc6ffdca031c20cba3b4fd66c77b_1675_1714))

Probably useful to move `IPV6_PROTO_PINFO` to packet-ipv6.h, and maybe a wrapper function to do the `curr_proto_layer_num` bit shifting.  I'll take a stab at it.
I wrote this before I wrote !25160 and I believe you're correct
